TOKENAMUN  what-if: caveman

compress agent-facing content the way Caveman claims to
Session carry-fixture, 8 API calls

Observed
  retrieved content                                 12.0 KB   [observed]
  eligible, delivered by a tool                      5.0 KB   [observed]
    of which opaque output                           1.1 KB   [observed]
      build logs and status noise: the cheap part to compress
    of which identifiable content                    3.9 KB   [observed]
      files the agent went looking for: compressing these is where a
      saving turns into extra tool calls
  eligible items                                          4   [observed]

Derived
  eligible content, estimated tokens                    842   [derived]
  carry cost of eligible content                      1,295   [derived]

Not measurable from this data
  Published figures span 8.5% to 65%.

Caveat
  An eight-fold spread; pick a number and you have made it up.
  Caveman's own figure is a 65% output reduction; an independent test
  measured 8.5% on real agentic tasks. On this session that is the
  difference between 110 tokens and 842 tokens. Neither was measured here,
  and which end applies depends on whether your tool output is build logs
  or content the agent went looking for. Use --replay-with to pipe this
  session's own output through the real compressor and settle it.

Unknown
  - additional_tool_calls: content the agent could no longer read may have
    been fetched again.
  - cache_invalidation_point: rewriting context breaks the cached prefix
    from that point, converting cheap reads into full-price writes. Where
    the change point cannot be determined this is not netted out.
  - behavioural_change: the agent's trajectory is assumed identical. It
    would not have been.
  - task_success: not observable from this data. An agent that fails the
    task consumes the fewest tokens of all, so a reduction is not an
    improvement.
